study_type_evidence.quote: Male C57BL/6J mice were administered an s.c. injection of either OT or PF-06655075 in a nondepot formulation.
Equilibrium dialysis using standard procedures were used for determination of the unbound fraction of OT and PF1 in rat plasma (fu,p) and rat brain homogenates (fu,b).
Binding assays were performed on membranes prepared from the Chinese hamster ovary hOTR NFAT βLac cell line.

in_vivo_species.quote: Male C57BL/6J mice (25–30g; Jackson Laboratories, Bar Harbor, ME) ... were maintained on a 12-hour light/dark cycle

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: male jugular vein cannulated Wistar Hannover, 250-300 g
in_vivo_species.quote: male jugular vein cannulated Wistar Hannover rats (250–300 g; Charles River Laboratories ...) were maintained on a 12-hour light/dark cycle

ex_vivo_detail: Equilibrium dialysis of rat plasma and rat brain homogenate to determine fraction unbound (fu,p = 0.0019 and fu,b = 0.0006 for PF1; fu,p = 0.89 for OT); dialysis incubation extended to 17 hours for PF1. Rat brain tissue and CSF harvested post-dose were also homogenized/processed for LC-MS/MS quantitation.
in_vitro_detail: Radioligand binding on CHO hOTR NFAT bLac cell membranes with [3H]8-arginine-vasopressin, and a calcium-flux FLIPR functional assay in stably transfected CHO hOTR NFAT bLac cells, to derive Ki and EC50 at OTR and V1a.

agents.name: Oxytocin (OT)
agents.sequence_source: Fig. 1a shows the structure of oxytocin; the body describes modifications by residue position (Pro7, Leu8) but prints no one-letter sequence
agents.chemical_identifier: purchased from Sigma-Aldrich (behavioral studies, Sigma no. 081M8715V) and from Phoenix Pharmaceuticals (pharmacokinetics)
agents.group_n: n = 3 per dose/compound (i.v. rat and s.c. nondepot mouse); n = 2 per dose/compound (s.c. depot mouse)
agents.group_n_quote: Individual animals (n = 3 per dose/compound) were administered a single s.c. injection based on body weight.

agents.dose_route_quote: The OT doses (1 and 10 mg/kg) were formulated in 20 mM phosphate buffered saline; PF1 (1 mg/kg) was formulated in 10% SEDDs

agents.cmax: 216 nM total (free Cmax = 191 nM) at 1 mg/kg s.c. nondepot; 65.4 nM total (free Cmax = 58.2 nM) at 20 mg/kg s.c. depot

agents.name: PF-06655075 (PF1)

agents.group_n: n = 3 per dose/compound (i.v. rat, s.c. nondepot mouse); n = 2 per dose/compound (s.c. depot mouse); n = 3 per time point (rat neuro-PK)

agents.pk_quote: s.c. administration of PF1 resulted in a total Cmax of 552 nM (free Cmax = 1.1 nM) and a half-life of 309 hours

bioanalytical_method: Protein precipitation followed by LC-MS/MS (AB Sciex API 5500 tandem quadrupole with TurboIon Spray, Acquity UPLC H-Class); non-compartmental analysis in Watson LIMS 7.4 and WinNonlin 5.2
bioanalytical_quote: Rat and mouse plasma and rat brain tissue and CSF were processed for quantitation of PF1 using protein precipitation followed by analysis using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).
bioanalytical_section: METHODS (Quantitation of Compound in Biologic Matrices)
notes: Mouse plasma half-lives are route/formulation dependent: OT 0.5 h (s.c. non-depot) and 7.3 h (s.c. depot, 20 mg/kg); PF1 3.2 h (s.c. non-depot, 1 mg/kg) and 309 h (s.c. depot, 20 mg/kg). Rat i.v. half-lives were 0.12 h (OT) and 8.5 h (PF1). Half-life values are reported without error terms. The i.v. dose of PF1 in rats is not numerically stated in the body (only the OT i.v. dose of 0.1 mg/kg is given). PF2 was tested ICV only and has no pharmacokinetic data. Mouse s.c. depot PK used only n = 2 per dose/compound.
